newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates rise before budget.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates rise before budget.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates rose on Wednesday on fresh buying before the national budget for fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) to be announced on Friday, dealers at the Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said.
Some spinners and exporters have bought cotton before the budget, a dealer said.
The rates were likely to fall on arrival of the new crop in the southern province of Sindh later this month, he said.
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was quoted for 2,125/2,225 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), the K-68 for 2,425/2,450 and the MNH-93 for 2,425/2,450.

The KCA said exporters had shipped 74,224 bales (375 lbs each) of cotton by May 28 compared to 1.81 million bales in the same time a year ago. Exporters had registered contracts for the export of 98,590 bales by June 4 compared to 2.32 million bales in the same time a year ago.
